t: Top 7 Causes of Dry Eye in Fort Myers and How Local Climate Affects Your Eyes
k: Top 7 Causes of Dry Eye in Fort Myers
x: Living in Southwest Florida comes with plenty of perks—sunshine, Gulf breezes, and an active outdoor lifestyle. However, many Fort Myers residents find that their eyes don't always feel as "tropical" as the weather. In fact, the unique climate of the Sunshine State can be surprisingly harsh on your tear film. At Riverside Family Eye Care, we see a high volume of patients seeking relief for dry eyes in Fort Myers. Understanding how our local environment impacts your vision is the first step toward lasting comfort. Here are the top seven causes of dry eye in our neck of the woods. 1. The "AC Trap" It sounds counterintuitive, but Florida’s humidity isn't always your friend. Because we spend so much time indoors to escape the heat, our eyes are constantly exposed to air conditioning. AC units act as dehumidifiers, stripping the moisture from the air and causing your tears to evaporate much faster than normal. 2. Intense UV Exposure The Southwest Florida sun is powerful. Constant exposure to UV rays without proper protection can lead to inflammation of the ocular surface. This inflammation disrupts the delicate balance of your tears, leading to chronic dry eye symptoms in Fort Myers. 3. Year-Round Allergies While other states have a "pollen season," Florida often feels like it has four. Between palm pollens, grasses, and mold, our local allergens can trigger allergic conjunctivitis. This causes redness and itching, which often masks or worsens underlying dry eye. 4. High Wind Exposure Whether you are boating on the Caloosahatchee or driving with the windows down, the constant flow of air across the surface of the eye accelerates tear evaporation. This is a common culprit for those who enjoy the "Riverside" lifestyle but suffer from grittiness afterward. 5. Digital Eye Strain Like everywhere else, Fort Myers professionals and retirees alike are spending more time on screens. When we look at phones or tablets, we blink up to 60% less often. This prevents the "meibomian glands" in your eyelids from releasing the essential oils needed to keep your eyes lubricated. 6. Chlorine and Saltwater Frequent dips in the pool or the Gulf are staples of Florida life. However, chlorine and salt can strip away the oily layer of your tear film, leaving your eyes feeling "hot" and irritated long after you’ve dried off. 7. Aging and Dehydration Our senior population is more susceptible to dry eye as tear production naturally declines with age. Combined with the Florida heat—which makes systemic dehydration a constant risk—your eyes can struggle to stay hydrated from the inside out. Practical Tips for Florida Residents Before your symptoms worsen, try these local lifestyle adjustments: The "Vents Down" Rule: Ensure your car's AC vents are pointed at your chest, not directly at your face. Invest in Wraparound Shades: High-quality, polarized sunglasses protect against both UV rays and the drying effects of the wind. Hydrate Constantly: In our climate, drinking water is essential for maintaining a healthy tear volume. When to See a Professional If you find yourself constantly reaching for over-the-counter drops, it’s time for a professional evaluation. Dry eyes from Florida weather often require more than just a standard artificial tear. At Riverside Family Eye Care, we use advanced diagnostics to determine exactly which layer of your tear film is failing and provide targeted treatments to help you get back to enjoying the Florida sun. Schedule Your Dry Eye Consultation Today
d: From AC to salt water, find out why Fort Myers residents struggle with dry eye symptoms. Get expert tips and professional relief for dry eyes in Fort Myers.

x: Our commitment and approach to maintaining an accessible website Our practice is committed to providing a website that is accessible to the widest possible audience, regardless of technology or ability. We have made every effort to make our website accessible and easy to use by following the available standards and guidelines. Website standards Our website seeks to conform with Worldwide Web Consortium (W3C) Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. In that regard, this website seeks to comply with Level AA and Level AAA compliance, as practicable. Accessibility features of this website Screen readers – To assist our visitors who are visually impaired or blind, our website is compatible with screen reading software. Code Compliance – This site was built using code compliant with W3C standards for HTML and CSS. Standards compliant code means that the site displays correctly in current browsers and ensures that it will display correctly in future browsers. Text Alternative – With the exception of decorative imagery, all non-text content presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. Screen readers can then present this alternate information to the user in place of the image. ARIA Landmarks – We use ARIA landmarks to identify regions of the page allowing those with screen readers to jump to different sections of the page. Skip to Main Content – Our pages all contain a skip to main content link allowing users to jump directly to the page’s main content, avoiding the header content from being read aloud repeatedly. Accessible Forms – Our forms have the proper markup to associate labels with their form controls making it easier for screen readers to present the form information to the user. Headings and Lists – We use the proper markup for headings and lists, i.e. h1-h6 and ol, ul and dl for lists. Heading markup will allow assistive technologies to present the heading status of text to a user. A screen reader can recognize the code and announce the text as a heading with its level, beep or provide some other auditory indicator. Some assistive technologies allow users to navigate from list to list or item to item. CSS – We use CSS to control visual presentation of text. This will allow users to modify, via the user agent, the visual characteristics of the text to meet their requirement. The text characteristics include aspects such as size, color, font family and relative placement. Resizing Text – Text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality. Raster Images – We avoid the use of text in raster images, this allows user agents to read aloud any text on the page and apply custom style sheets to make the text more legible. Keyboard Interface – The site is designed with consideration for people unable to use a mouse. The website can be navigated using your computer’s keyboard or by using other assistive devices. All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystroked. When all functionality of content can be operated through a keyboard or keyboard interface, it can be operated by those with no vision as well as by those who must use alternate keyboards or input devices that act as keyboard emulators like speech input software or on-screen keyboards. Flashing Content – Web pages do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period, or the flash is below the general flash and red flash thresholds. These effects are known to cause seizures if the flashes are bright and large enough. Page Titles – Our web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose. Descriptive titles help users find content, orient themselves within it, and navigate through it. A descriptive title allows a user to easily identify what Web page they are using and to tell when the Web page has changed. The title can be used to identify the Web page without requiring users to read or interpret page content. Users can more quickly identify the content they need when accurate, descriptive titles appear in site maps or lists of search results. When descriptive titles are used within link text, they help users navigate more precisely to the content they are interested in. Locating Content – More than one way is available to locate a Web page within a set of Web pages. We provide breadcrumbs, and site maps. This makes it possible for users to locate content in a manner that best meets their needs. Users may find one technique easier or more comprehensible to use than another. Highlighting – The majority of our web site components allow for highlighting by the user agent when they receive focus. Default Language – The default human language of each Web page can be programmatically determined. Speech synthesizers that support multiple languages will be able to orient and adapt to the pronunciation and syntax that are specific to the language of the page, speaking the text in the appropriate accent with proper pronunciation. Component Focus – When any of our components receive focus, they do not initiate a change of context, i.e. forms submitted automatically when a component receives focus, new windows launched when a component receives focus. Consistent Navigation – We have a consistent navigation across our web pages. This technique makes the placement of navigational components more predictable. Form Input Errors – In forms, if an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text. Proper Coding – Elements have complete start and end tags, elements are nested according to their specifications, elements do not contain duplicate attributes, and any IDs are unique. These errors that are known to cause problems for assistive technologies when they are trying to parse content which involve having opening and closing tags that are not used according to specification. Portable Document Format (PDFs) – Some documents on this website are in PDF format. You need Adobe Acrobat to open these files. You can download Acrobat for free. Download Adobe Acrobat. Exceptions While we strive to adhere to the accepted guidelines and the highest standards for accessibility and usability, it is not always possible to do so in all areas of the website. Future Efforts We are currently working to achieve Level AA and Level AAA conformance to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0, as practicable. How to send feedback on this website’s accessibility We welcome feedback on the accessibility of this website or if, for any reason, you are unable to access any part of this website, please contact us immediately. Email us at: optician@riversidefamilyeyecare.com Phone us at: 239-500-2020 Write to us at: 11841 Palm Beach Blvd, Unit 117 Fort Myers FL

x: Living in Fort Myers means plenty of sun and salt air, but it should not mean living with a constant gritty feeling in eyes. If you find yourself reaching for eye drops just to get through the afternoon, you are likely dealing with more than temporary irritation. At Riverside Family Eye Care, dry eye specialist in Fort Myers Dr. Brittany Degler provides a personalized dry eye treatment plan that starts with a sophisticated, data-driven dry eye assessment. Identifying Your Specific Type of Dry Eye Dry eye is not a single diagnosis; it is a clinical puzzle. Our primary goal is to stop the guessing game and pinpoint your specific subtype, such as Meibomian Gland Dysfunction (MGD). If we do not identify which layer of your tear film is struggling, any treatment is merely a guess. We use advanced imaging to treat the root cause of dry eye intelligently, ensuring your dry eye exam in Fort Myers leads to actual relief rather than just masking symptoms. A Non-Invasive Dry Eye Exam: What to Expect Many patients ask, "what happens during a dry eye exam?" The process is streamlined and entirely comfortable. Specialized Imaging: You simply blink into a machine that captures high-resolution images of your tear-producing glands. Gentle Indicators: Dr. Degler uses diagnostic dyes like fluorescein to highlight dry spots. These are medical-grade indicators that do not sting. Objective Data: These tests provide a clear view of your ocular surface that goes far beyond a verbal description of symptoms. Your Comfort and Convenience If you have a fear of the unknown regarding eye exams, rest easy. This is a non-invasive dry eye exam. There are no needles, no scratching, and no dilation is required. You can return to your daily activities in Fort Myers immediately after your appointment without blurred vision or light sensitivity. The Step-Wise Philosophy: Our Conservative Ladder Dr. Degler utilizes a step-wise ladder for doctor-guided dry eye care. We rarely jump to advanced procedures on day one. Instead, we begin with "homework"—a tailored regimen of: High-quality warm compresses. The best artificial tears for dry eyes specific to your tear film deficiency. Professional-grade Omega-3 supplements. We typically allow three to four months for these conservative management strategies to support your natural tear production. x: Your eyes are your windows to the soul and the world, maintaining their health is vital for your overall well-being. Certain eye conditions, like cataracts, glaucoma, dry eye syndrome, and age-related macular degeneration, can significantly impair your vision and quality of life. At Riverside Family Eye Care, we emphasize the importance of regular eye exams to detect and manage these conditions early, helping to preserve your sight. Cataracts: A Leading Cause of Vision Loss Cataracts develop when the natural lens of the eye becomes cloudy, leading to blurred vision and, if left untreated, significant vision loss. This condition often develops slowly and may not be noticeable in the initial stages Regular eye exams at Riverside Family Eye Care allow us to monitor the progression of cataracts and determine the best time for intervention, such as cataract surgery, to restore clear vision. Glaucoma: The Silent Thief of Sight Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that damage the optic nerve, often due to increased pressure in the eye. This condition is particularly dangerous because it typically presents no symptoms until significant vision loss has occurred. Regular visits with us are critical for early detection through tests that measure intraocular pressure and assess the health of the optic nerve. Early treatment can prevent further damage and protect your vision – for more information on the silent thief of sight, look at some of our additional reading on glaucoma. Dry Eye Syndrome: Chronic Discomfort and Vision Issues Dry eye syndrome occurs when your eyes do not produce enough tears or when the tears evaporate too quickly. This can lead to chronic discomfort, blurred vision, and increased risk of eye infections. Managing dry eye requires a comprehensive approach, including the use of artificial tears, prescription medications or more advanced treatments available at Riverside Family Eye Care. Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD): Protecting Central Vision AMD affects the macula, the part of the retina responsible for sharp central vision. This condition is a leading cause of blindness in older adults and can significantly impact daily activities like reading and driving. While there is no cure for AMD, early detection through regular eye exams at Riverside Family Eye Care allows for timely intervention, such as lifestyle changes, nutritional supplements, or specialized treatments to slow its progression. The Importance of Regular Eye Exams Regular visits to your optometrist are essential for maintaining eye health and preventing vision loss from these serious conditions. At Riverside Family Eye Care, we pride ourselves in providing comprehensive eye care tailored to your needs. t: This Winter, Don’t Let Dry Eyes Get the Best of You
h: Get Dry Eye Relief at Riverside Family Eye Care
x: The sharp, dry winds and cold air of winter can cause or worsen dry eye symptoms. So can indoor heating, which sucks out moisture. While many of us can't completely avoid wintry weather, there are things we can do to minimize dry eyes, as well as a variety of ways to treat it. What is Dry Eye? Dry eye syndrome (DES) is caused by a lack of tears or poor quality tears, leading to irritation and discomfort in the eyes. Dry eye syndrome can be annoying and, left untreated, severe cases can damage the surface of the eye and even lead to vision loss. That's why it's so important to understand what causes DES and to treat it. What Causes Dry Eye Syndrome? Dry eye syndrome can be caused by aging, certain medications and medical conditions, and excessive screen time (we blink less when staring at a digital screen). Other causes include vision correction surgery, and smoking. Your environment can also be the culprit. Indoor heating dries out the eyes, and the same is true of cold air and dry winds. Is it any wonder that dry eye symptoms peak during the winter and any time it's cold? Fortunately, there are ways to reduce dry eye symptoms. Dry Eye Prevention and Treatment Following a dry eye consult, your eye doctor will recommend ways to treat the condition. Usually, artificial tears, over-the-counter eye drops or prescription drops are the first line of defense. They may be combined with in-office dry eye treatments. In addition, eating foods rich in omega-3 fatty acids, using a humidifier, maintaining eyelid hygiene and applying warm compresses to your eyes as directed by your eye doctor can help alleviate symptoms. x: In Fort Myers offices and home workspaces, the first few hours of the day often set the tone for mounting eye strain. By midday, your screen can feel harsher than the morning light through the window, and the words on the page may blur or shimmer. Remote professionals across the city feel it too, especially during those stretches when one meeting ends and the next one begins before your eyes catch their breath. March is Workplace Eye Wellness Month. This is a timely reminder to pay attention to the subtle signs of eye strain at work that build up after hours of close-up work. At Riverside Family Eye Care, we help patients understand why their eyes feel strained and what adjustments can bring real relief. Our comprehensive eye exams support clearer, more comfortable vision at every stage of life. If dryness is part of the problem, our dry eye care services provide targeted evaluation and treatment to restore moisture and comfort throughout your day. Why Workplace Eye Comfort Matters Most days, it feels like your eyes never get a moment away from screens, whether you’re answering messages, reviewing reports, or jumping into another video call. Office teams downtown move from dashboards to emails, while remote professionals across Fort Myers shift between laptops, tablets, and phones. Each transition requires your eyes to refocus, adjust to changing brightness, and maintain steady near vision for extended periods. Over time, these patterns lead to symptoms often grouped under computer vision syndrome, a common issue for today’s screen-heavy routines. When your eyes work harder than they should, your energy dips, and routine tasks feel more demanding. As the day continues, vision changes can interrupt your focus and make work feel heavier than it should. Recognizing early signs of strain gives you the chance to make small changes that protect your vision and help you move through your workday with greater ease. How to Set Up a Vision-Friendly Workstation A few thoughtful adjustments to your office ergonomics for eyes can reduce the strain that builds during long hours at a desk. Consider these simple strategies: Follow the 20-20-20 rule. Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds to give your eyes a short reset. Position your monitor so your gaze falls slightly downward. This natural angle reduces tension and supports a more relaxed focus. Minimize glare by adjusting overhead lighting or using softer light sources that feel comfortable rather than sharp. Maintain a steady posture. A balanced spine and grounded feet help your eyes settle, which often brings a sense of ease as you work. Choose lenses with an anti-reflective coating to reduce harsh reflections and visual fatigue. Blue light glasses may also help reduce work from home eye strain, especially in home offices where lighting shifts throughout the afternoon. Signs Your Eyes May Need an Updated Prescription Even with an optimized workspace, persistent strain can signal that your prescription has changed. Many Fort Myers professionals notice the same gradual clues. Text loses crispness. Headaches appear after long stretches of computer work. Tasks that once felt effortless now leave your eyes tired. Common signs include: Frequent headaches during or after screen use Blurred or fluctuating vision Dry, irritated eyes Difficulty maintaining focus on detailed work A comprehensive eye exam can determine whether your prescription needs updating or if your eyes require more tailored support for digital work. Updated lenses or customized solutions often provide noticeable relief. At Riverside Family Eye Care, we use careful testing to make sure your prescription supports long workdays and long-term eye comfort.
